page: Microsoft Azure B1ms is a burstable virtual machine belonging to the BS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a single vCPU mapped to one physical core and one thread, powered by an Intel Xeon 8171M processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and 50 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 2.0 GB of system memory and 4 GB of local storage, with support for Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates that the B1ms is positioned at the lower end of the performance spectrum. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests both yield a score of 1224.89, reflecting its single-threaded limitation. Memory bandwidth is constrained, with read-only large block transfers at 9.24 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 7.48 GB/sec. Passmark CPU and memory scores are 1459.16 and 919.77 respectively, while Redis SET operations reach 1.5 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the B1ms offers a low-cost entry point for workloads that do not require continuous full CPU utilization. The burstable CPU allocation model allows the server to accumulate credits during idle periods to handle occasional spikes in demand. However, the primary tradeoff is the strict resource limitation, as sustained high CPU usage will deplete credits and throttle performance, and the 2.0 GB memory capacity limits the execution of memory-intensive applications.

This server configuration is suitable for lightweight, non-critical workloads. Appropriate use cases include small-scale static web serving, basic development or testing environments, minor database operations, and simple background scripting tasks that can tolerate variable CPU performance.
